name: BEML Ltd
tagline: Defence + mining-equipment + rail-coach PSU with a large order pipeline and a land-monetisation angle, but structurally low returns and an extreme multiple - a large-cap, not a screen fit
business_overview: BEML (Government of India ~54%) makes heavy earth-moving equipment for mining and construction, defence vehicles and aggregates, and metro/Rail coaches. A separate demerged entity, BEML Land Assets Ltd (BLAL), holds ~550 acres of surplus Bengaluru/Mysuru land for eventual monetisation. Management cites a ~Rs 40,000 Cr pipeline across ~6 domestic projects plus two large metro export opportunities, even after the ~Rs 20,000 Cr MRVC tender was cancelled.
fundamentals_narrative: Returns are structurally weak for a capital-goods PSU (7.7% ROCE, 4.9% ROE) and five-year sales growth is ~4%. Debt is low and debtor days are high (~191). At ~92x earnings the stock already discounts a large order-book conversion and a successful disinvestment/land story. This is a genuine large-cap where the size math alone makes a 10x/100x outcome implausible.
technical_read: Not pulled - not a Tier-A candidate. CMP is mid-range of the 52-week band.

No recent activity, no roster-user conviction call. Source is a trusted-x-watch snippet mention (@a_basumallick concall note, 2026-08-20), not a stated position.

bull_case: ~Rs 40,000 Cr stated pipeline (defence, metro, mining) plus two metro export opportunities gives multi-year order visibility
Defence indigenisation and metro-rail capex are real multi-year tailwinds for a domestic OEM
Surplus land in BLAL is a separate, if slow, value-unlock; low debt
Recurring disinvestment chatter is a periodic re-rating trigger
bear_case: Genuine large-cap (Rs 16,376 Cr) - 10x/2-3yr or 100x/10yr is not on the table on size math
Structurally low returns (7.7% ROCE, 4.9% ROE) and ~4% 5-yr sales growth - order pipelines have historically not converted into earnings power
~92x P/E already prices the order book and the land/disinvestment optionality
PSU execution, high debtor days (~191), and a just-cancelled Rs 20,000 Cr tender show pipeline-to-revenue slippage
The land-monetisation angle (via BLAL) is timing-uncertain and typically realises below market
